metricDefinitions.label: Inventory value
metricDefinitions.definition: Physical quantity on hand multiplied by unit cost. Reservations, backorders, and open purchase orders do not change this value.

metricDefinitions.label: Available quantity
metricDefinitions.definition: Physical quantity on hand minus reserved quantity, floored at zero. Stock status, days of stock, and replenishment use this amount.

metricDefinitions.label: Monthly usage
metricDefinitions.definition: Sale quantity in the final 30 days of the complete 90-day window. It is measured in each product's listed unit.

metricDefinitions.label: Needs replenishment
metricDefinitions.definition: A positive customer backorder, available quantity at or below the reorder level, or estimated days of available stock at or below supplier lead time.

metricDefinitions.label: Suggested top-up
metricDefinitions.definition: For a product needing replenishment with final-30-day sales or known backorder demand: target stock plus backorder quantity minus available quantity minus open purchase-order quantity, floored at zero. Backorders and reservations are separate inputs.

metricDefinitions.label: Overstock
metricDefinitions.definition: Physical quantity above the product maximum stock level. Overstock value is only the excess quantity multiplied by unit cost.

metricDefinitions.label: Backorder
metricDefinitions.definition: A product with positive unmet customer demand. Headline counts report affected products; quantities are shown only per product because listed units differ.

metricDefinitions.label: Slow-moving / non-moving
metricDefinitions.definition: Positive physical stock whose most recent Sale or Receipt was 30–59 / at least 60 days before the snapshot. No movement in the complete history is reported as at least 90 days.

metricDefinitions.label: Needs attention
metricDefinitions.definition: A distinct product with an expiry, backorder, purchasing, overstock, slow-moving, or non-moving reason. Priority is expired, backorder, stockout purchasing, near expiry, other purchasing, then excess or stale stock.

caveats: Harborline, its products, transactions, suppliers, reservations, backorders and purchase orders are fictional demonstration data.
The stock snapshot is September 11, 2026. The complete 90-day history starts June 14, 2026. All products existed throughout this period.
Unit costs are held constant throughout the sample history. Quantities use each product's listed unit and are never totaled across unlike products.
Reservations reduce available quantity but do not change physical quantity, inventory value, or the historical stock rollforward.
Backorders represent unmet customer demand. They are separate from open purchase orders, which represent incoming supply.
Expiry uses one date for all currently-held units of a tracked product; batches are not modeled. Expired units remain in physical and available stock until an explicit stock movement removes them.
Maximum stock, reserved quantity, and customer backorder quantity are product-level planning inputs in the Inventory tab.
